study.question: Does an uncompressed history-value path improve two-round field/history exchange after count scaling, and does its value depend on refreshed queries? Observations: DIN click AUC=0.655544; original exchange q1/w1=0.647458, q0/w1=0.645457, q1/w0=0.640740, q0/w0=0.632297. Mass m1/q1=0.653330 versus m0/q1=0.640630, and m1/q0=0.651864 versus m0/q0=0.640878. Count scaling helped in both query conditions, but every exchange trial still loses to DIN. For long histories, DIN=0.657803 versus mass m1/q1=0.653757; buy AUC also trails 0.870182 versus 0.857668. These are single-seed observations, not repeated support. All nine executions succeeded; no execution failure is inferred from a predictive loss.
study.hypothesis: The remaining deficit may partly reflect discarding original field/action embedding directions through the event projection and normalization, independently of count scale. Let W2 be the second strict-masked, sqrt(n)-scaled attention matrix, and H the original concatenated history embeddings (six item fields plus action, Dv=112 at embedding_dim=16). Compute s=mean_fields(W2) H. Both treatments expose a learned linear rank-32 reconstruction U D s to otherwise identical towers; the candidate adds the parameter-free identity residual s. This preserves direct value information while keeping field-conditioned retrieval in the evolving low-dimensional exchange state. Query refresh Q is crossed with the value residual R. A positive R effect supports this particular direct value route; a positive R-by-Q interaction is separately needed to support their complementarity. It does not prove a global rank bound on the original field stack or establish a novel mechanism.

nearest_work.difference: Archived exact-version primary text, lines 250-277: target-dependent weighted sums of original embeddings and unnormalized weights. We inherit the idea of preserving embedding values, but use mean field-query attention after two exchange rounds, strict masked softmax times sqrt(n), and a raw residual versus learned rank-32 reconstruction. This is not exact DIN reproduction.

Pinned benchmark source lines 198-282 uses repeated cross-attention with shared sequence K/V and token-specific query/output matrices. We retain repeated retrieval from our local family, use shared query/output projections and field mixers, and expose original embedding values outside the 32-channel state. No EST heterogeneous FFNs or reproduction claim.

Pinned benchmark source lines 241-313 aggregates hubs and broadcasts affine signals. Our inherited field-mean affine event writer is fixed in all cells; no task hubs, task routing, or mask-free attention. Its contribution is not re-estimated here.

Section 2.3 identifies EST/INFNet layer-wise interaction and UniMixer raw-history flattening. We keep event retrieval and add a compact pooled value route rather than flattening all 100 events into a tokenizer. Original EST/INFNet paper detail is unavailable through the registry; novelty relative to those papers remains unverified.

study.proposed_difference: Return existing attention weights from each reader. At the second read, average weights over field queries and pool original masked history embeddings into one 112-dimensional vector. Pass it through bias-free 112->32->112 linear layers in every cell. R=1 adds the original pooled vector to the reconstruction; R=0 exposes only the reconstruction. Append the resulting 112 values to the same tower inputs in all four cells. Q=1 uses first_fields for the second read; Q=0 reuses first_query, exactly as in the prior factorial. The writer remains active in both Q conditions, so Q=0 is a fixed-query control, not absence of all iterative exchange. The raw route reads original embeddings, not rewritten events; only selection weights depend on rewritten events. All four modules instantiate the same parameters in the same order, and all learned modules remain active. Sparse widths and loss are unchanged.
predictions: Primary predeclared contrasts: dR_Q1=AUC(value_r1_q1)-AUC(value_r0_q1) and dR_Q0=AUC(value_r1_q0)-AUC(value_r0_q0). Positive values in both cells would support local value preservation more strongly than a gain only against the old narrower-head ancestor.
Complementarity contrast I=dR_Q1-dR_Q0 is predicted positive. If I is nonpositive, report no support for value-preservation/query-refresh synergy even if R improves prediction.

Quality target: value_r1_q1 exceeds the ancestor 0.653330 and preferably DIN 0.655544 in full-population click AUC. All four task AUC/Logloss and cost remain necessary; a click gain with worse auxiliary performance is a tradeoff, not uniform improvement.

Exploratory localization: inspect the already established empty,1-16,17-64,>64 history bins with sample/positive/negative counts (negative=samples-positives). The ancestor >64 deficit motivates inspection but no unique long-history response is required. Empty histories have s=0 exactly before training; trained models can nevertheless differ there through globally learned weights. Do not invent unavailable frequency/composition diagnostics.

All four variants have identical learned parameter counts and tower shapes; with Dv112, predicted delta to ancestor is 2*112*32 + 4*112*128 = 64512 dense parameters: total32378628/dense585412/embedding31793216. Confirm host counts. Memory and latency need measurement; equal parameters do not imply equal effective capacity or equal compute.
falsifiers: Both matched R effects are nonpositive: no local support for this direct raw-value residual implementation; do not conclude all value-preserving mechanisms are ineffective.
Only the rank-32 controls improve versus the ancestor: the larger common readout or a new value aggregation path can explain the family gain; the raw identity residual lacks support.
Interaction I<=0: the proposed complementarity is unsupported, even if the residual has a useful main effect.
Nonfinite empty-history output, padding-value sensitivity, wrong task output shape or host resource-cap violation invalidates the implementation before predictive interpretation.
If all cells remain below DIN or cost rises without useful quality, retain DIN as incumbent; a controlled mechanistic contrast within a losing family is not a successful replacement.
alternative_explanations: Identity addition changes scale, conditioning, initialization geometry and implicit regularization, as well as bypassing a rank-32 map. This batch identifies the composite residual route, not pure information rank. A scale-matched or fixed full-rank transform replacement would be a discriminating follow-up if it wins.
The common extra rank-32 reconstruction and wider tower can explain improvement relative to old trials. Use within-batch R contrasts for attribution; old trials are historical anchors only.
Averaging field-query weights may dilute target-specific evidence; failed raw pooling would not refute per-field raw-value access.
Existing field states retain multiple query summaries and raw current fields, so compressing each event to32 is not proof of a global32-dimensional information bottleneck.

One seed, adaptive selection of the question from validation, rare auxiliary positives and repeated user exposures limit uncertainty claims. No user-cluster confidence interval or significance claim is fabricated.
